newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says it won't be scapegoat for Hebron delay.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says it won't be scapegoat for Hebron delay.

text.p: Egypt said on Saturday it refused to take the blame for delays in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on an Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said the only reason for delay was that the Palestinians had not yet received proposals they could accept on a long-delayed Israeli withdrawal.

He was answering a question on Israeli allegations that Egypt was inciting the Palestinians not to sign. Israel complained last month of Egypt's role on the sidelines of the talks but it was not clear if or when it had complained again.
"This is nonsense and baseless," Moussa told reporters. "The Palestinians know when to accept and what to accept."

President Hosni Mubarak, in a closed-door meeting with selected Egyptian journalists, also denied that Egypt was trying to make changes to the original agreement on Hebron, signed more than a year ago but never implemented.
"There is no truth in what is being said that Egypt is trying to add new clauses," said Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif, quoting Mubarak.
"Egypt's position is clear and it is to respect the agreement signed by the Palestinians and Israelis," he added.

Moussa said: "What is obstructing the agreement so far is that there are no proposals which the Palestinians can accept, even if there has been great progress. But there are some points which still fall short of being balanced, just and fair."
"This policy of blaming things on others is unacceptable to us. Anyone who says there is incitement by Egypt is finding excuses for failure, delay and procrastination," he added.
Commenting on the incident in which an Israeli soldier opened fire at Palestinians in Hebron market on Wednesday, Moussa said Arabs needed the same security as Israelis.
"It matters to us that security be for everyone, not for one side at the expense of the other, because that would not be security and would not help maintain security," he added.
The minister also condemned the bus bomb which killed nine people and wounded 44 in Damascus on Tuesday.
"There's no doubt this was a terrorist act targeting civilians and this is unacceptable," Moussa added.
